questions.question: State three purposes of a trial balance and the rule for which column each balance is placed in.
questions.expected_answer: Purposes: to check the arithmetical accuracy of the double entry (debits equal credits); to summarise all ledger balances on one page; to serve as the basis for preparing the financial statements. Debit column: assets, expenses and drawings; credit column: capital, liabilities and income.

questions.question: Show that Ridgeview Hardware's trial balance balances, given debit balances of R2 000, R7 500, R10 600, R83 660, R18 400, R5 000, R12 000, R850 and R240, and credit balances of R80 000, R30 000, R27 600, R2 500 and R150.
Name two errors that a trial balance will reveal and two that it will not reveal, with an example of each.
questions.expected_answer: Revealed (any two): one-sided posting (cost of sales debited but trading stock not credited); posting to the wrong side; different amounts posted (telephone R850 posted as R580); incorrect addition or balancing; an account omitted from the trial balance. Not revealed (any two): omission (transaction not recorded at all); commission (telephone posted to stationery); principle (equipment debited to trading stock); original entry (wrong amount in the journal); compensating errors; reversal of entries.
